title: The Value column silently switches from the Hill-curve board to the raw scraper composite for 260 rows, and 158 of them display a LARGER number than the deepest genuinely-priced player
rootCause: `_materializePlayerArrayRow` sets `full: Math.round(backendValue || rawValues.full)` where `rawValues.full = displayValue || finalAdjusted || overall`. When the canonical pipeline declines to price a row it stamps `rankDerivedValue: null` and `values.displayValue: null`, leaving `values.overall`/`values.finalAdjusted` holding the pre-pipeline scraper composite. The client promotes that number into the same column, with the same formatting, the same value-band badge and the same sort key as real Hill values.
evidence: frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1008 — `full: Math.round(backendValue || rawValues.full),` and the render at frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1050 — `const val = Math.round(row.rankDerivedValue || row.values?.full || 0);`. Live contract: Devin Bush `values={overall:2549, rawComposite:2549, finalAdjusted:2549, displayValue:null}`, `rankDerivedValue:null` → row displays 2,549, band 'D — Depth value (2000-3999)'. Malachi Moore, the last backend-ranked player (#740): `rankDerivedValue:757` → displays 757, band 'F — Fringe'. 260 of 1,072 rows take the fallback; 249 display a non-zero value; 158 display more than 757.
userImpact: A user sorting or scanning by Value sees Devin Bush (a rotational LB the pipeline refused to price) at 2,549 — 3.4× the value of the deepest player the model actually priced. Sorting the board by Value descending places him at display position 224, interleaved among real top-225 assets while his rank cell reads '#905'. Any trade evaluated off the displayed number for one of these 216 players is evaluated on a scale the trade engines never use — `finder.py`, `suggestions.py`, `angle.py` and `waiver.py` all read `rankDerivedValue`, which is null here. The CSV export carries the same mixed column with no marker.

rootCause: There is no single stated convention for what `sides[i].assets` means in a 2-team trade, and the codebase implements both. The verdict label picked one; the flow math, the stack lens, the simulator hand-off, the 3+-team meter and the side-card labels picked the other.
evidence:
GIVE convention — frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:1392-1393 `const value = ...effectiveValue(asset...); result[i].given += value;` then `result[dest].received += value`; frontend/app/trade/trade-sections.jsx:808 `
Giving
` over `side.assets`; frontend/components/graphs/MultiTradeFlow.jsx:80 "Each side appears once on the left (giver)"; frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1313-1319 "Whichever side has more matches is 'my side' (I'm giving)" → those names are sent as `playersOut`; page.jsx:1587 applySuggestion puts the backend's `give` list on side 0. WIN-IS-BIGGER convention — frontend/components/trade/TradeMeter.jsx:37,58-60 `const gap = pwA - pwB; ... winnerText = gap > 0 ? \`${labelA} wins by ${pctGap}%\``; TradeFairnessExplanation.jsx:135 `const winnerLabel = overallGap > 0 ? labelA : labelB;`; page.jsx:2084-2085 `
{verdictFromGap(pwGap)}` with colorFromGap green for gap>0. The arithmetic settles which reading the math uses: trade-logic.js:843 `adjusted: rawA + adjA - stackA` subtracts a side's own stack GAIN, while :1421 `net = received - given + stack[i]` adds it — the two are consistent only if `adjusted` is a give-total. In 2-team mode nothing on screen says which it is: the 'Giving'/'Receiving' labels render only when `sides.length > 2` (trade-sections.jsx:807, 836).
userImpact: Executed on the real module: sides A=[9000] vs B=[6000] produce `gap = +3000` → the sticky tray and meter show green on Side A and 'Side A wins by 33%', while `computeSideFlows` on the identical input returns `net_A = -3000` and the 3-side meter would render Side A as 'Losing value' in red. rootCause: analyzeRawTrade values every asset at the current board; gradeRetro was layered on top as a badge instead of replacing the grade, and its own at-trade leg is incomplete.
evidence: frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:132 `value: row.values?.full || 0` (picks) and :146 `const baseVal = row.values?.full || 0` (players) — the live contract's current value. The headline is built from that: :394-395 `const pctGap = (netAdjusted / scale) * 100; const grade = gradeTradeHistorySide(...)`, rendered at frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:225-232 as '<team> won by X%' with letter grades from league-analysis.js:87-98. userImpact: Every 'A+ / Fleeced / won by 38%' verdict on /trades is retrodiction: a player who broke out after the trade makes the acquirer look prescient and the sender look robbed, when at the time the deal may have been even. title: Balancing suggestions are sized against a VA-inclusive gap but selected by raw value, so the suggested piece does not close the gap
rootCause: findBalancers treats the gap as a linear quantity, but adding a piece changes the piece counts that drive the Value Adjustment.
evidence: frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:756 `const list = findBalancers(pwGap, pool, valueMode);` where `pwGap` comes from the adjusted totals (:708-712). frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:1256-1260 selects purely on `Number(r.values?.[valueMode] || 0)` sorted by `Math.abs(a.value - target)`. userImpact: On any 1-for-many shape, following the app's own balancing advice can move the verdict further from even, and the user has no way to see why.

userImpact: Bluntly: this is the best-evidenced system in the audit and it does not need a false-positive rate, because it asserts nothing falsifiable — every number is a count of a public transaction, with the underlying movements one click away. title: The waiver comparison subtracts raw scraper-composite values from canonical board values, and every headline drop recommendation is one of those rows
rootCause: rowValue falls back to values.full when rankDerivedValue is absent (waiver-logic.js:196-205). On the default view=app payload buildRows takes the legacy-dict branch (server.py:1953-1954 strips playersArray from the runtime view), where values.full = rankDerivedValue || rawValues.full - i.e. _finalAdjusted, the raw scraper composite. The candidate pool guards against this (rowHasNoRealRank + sourceCount<2 at waiver-logic.js:341,363) but the ROSTER side applies neither gate (waiver-logic.js:547-554 checks only assetClass=='pick' and rowValue<=0).
evidence: waiver-logic.js:201-204 - `const v = Number(row?.rankDerivedValue); if (Number.isFinite(v) && v > 0) return v; const v2 = Number(row?.values?.full); return ...`. Executed against the real contract with the real buildRows on a runtime-shaped payload: 12 of team Blaine's 52 matched roster rows carry rankDerivedValue null and are priced off _finalAdjusted (AJ Haulcy 1954, Divine Deablo 1913, James Pearce 1907, Cole Bishop 1876, Mack Hollins 1107, Derek Carr 888, Colton Hood 497...). The resulting top-5 Droppable rows are Colton Hood 497, Caden Curry 510, Dante McClellan 515, Bryan Thompson 744, Isaiah Williams 744 - ALL unstamped fallback rows. Scale mismatch over the 805 players carrying both numbers: _finalAdjusted/rankDerivedValue median 1.099, p10 0.958, p90 1.268, max 1.704.
userImpact: Every 'Drop X' the page leads with is a number the canonical pipeline declined to stamp, subtracted from a canonical number to produce the net gain and the tier badge. The gating is one-sided: an unstamped player can only ever be DROPPED, never ADDED. The headline tier flips on this alone - with the fallback rows in, the top move is 'strong' (net 1273); with them out, 'considering' (net 848). title: The Monte Carlo trade simulator's uncertainty is a hardcoded ±15% for every asset, because the real band producer has no caller
rootCause: monte_carlo.py was written to consume per-player p10/p50/p90 bands from Phase 4 confidence intervals. The frontend duplicates it at frontend/components/ui/MonteCarloButton.jsx:55-57 — `p10 = v * 0.85; p50 = v; p90 = v * 1.15;`. We sample 20,000 times from this disagreement range". src/trade/monte_carlo.py:8 repeats the claim ("each with a ``valueBand`` from Phase 4"). area: Trade engines: src/trade/ (15 modules, ~8,200 LOC) + src/api/trade_simulator.py + routes /api/trade/{suggestions,finder,simulate,simulate-mc,import-ktc,export-k
title: The finder applies KTC's package Value Adjustment to the market side only, never to the board side — manufacturing arbitrage out of a scale asymmetry
evidence: src/trade/finder_value_adjustment.py:44 `adjusted[index] = replace(adjusted[index], market_value=value + adjustment)` — only `market_value` is replaced; `model_value` is untouched, and finder.py:641-643 sums `_mv(a)` (the board value) raw. Live top result, verified end-to-end: give Josh Allen (board 9,993 / KTC 9,987), receive Joe Burrow + Patrick Mahomes (board 8,428 + 7,488 = 15,916 / KTC 7,395 + 6,307 = 13,702). rawGiveKtcTotal 9,987 → giveKtcTotal 13,850 after marketValueAdjustment +3,863; opponentKtcAppeal +0.011; boardDelta +5,923. Applying the SAME algorithm to the board values gives +1,820, which would cut boardDelta from 5,923 to 4,103. Across all 12 teams: 441 of 449 returned trades (98.2%) carried marketValueAdjustmentApplied.

title: tradePartnerFitScore ships a reachable range of [7.24, 43.12] that is unreachable through the only wiring that serves it; measured live ceiling is 16.37
evidence: `src/roster_intel/partner.py:536-573` `_reachable_fit_bounds()` derives the published bounds assuming `max_conf=0.40` (HISTORY_INFORMED) and full 3/3 structural coverage. `src/api/gameplan.py:915-926` constructs `PartnerInputs` with **no** `shape`, no `trades_completed`, no `league_mean_trades`, no `pair_trades_completed` → `_fairness_term` and `_history_term` both abstain → tier is SHAPE_ONLY (0.30), `measured = 2/3` → `confidence = 0.30 * (0.55 + 0.45*0.6667) = 0.2550` for every partner, always. Measured live (real 12-team bundle, owner 468418790212759552): all 11 partners have `acceptanceConfidence == 0.255` exactly, and fit scores span 10.48 … 16.37 against the shipped `tradePartnerFitScoreRange` of `{min: 7.24, max: 43.12}`.
userImpact: The bounds were added specifically so a renderer would not draw a good partner as a failing grade — and under the real wiring the best partner draws at 38% of the shipped gauge. `acceptanceConfidence` is a constant wearing a score's clothes: it varies with nothing.

title: The server-side adjusted contract scales only rankDerivedValue, leaving offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue and values.* at market — suggestions.py mixes both scales in one comparison
evidence: src/league_intel/overlay.py:88-95 scales exactly one field: `copy["rankDerivedValue"] = int(round(base * factor))`. The client-side applier does more — frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1911-1917 also scales `values.overall|finalAdjusted|displayValue` and :1946 `_finalAdjusted`. Meanwhile src/trade/suggestions.py:626-643 reads `row["offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue"]` into `offense_only_value`, and :765-769 `_eff_val` returns that unscaled number for offensive positions while returning the SCALED `display_value` for IDP positions (:1089-1099, :1251-1294 pass `pos_oo = pos not in _IDP_BASE_POSITIONS`). On the live contract 607 of 1092 rows carry a positive `offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue`.
userImpact: CLAUDE.md's central justification for the whole overlay design — "every engine reads exactly one value — rankDerivedValue" — is false. Under `valuationMode=leagueAdjusted`, the upgrade and depth searches in trade suggestions compare adjusted IDP values against unadjusted offense values, a scale mismatch of up to 5.3% that silently biases which upgrades and sweeteners are proposed.

area: Data ingestion, source registry, and normalization pipeline — Dynasty Scraper.py + scripts/fetch_*.py + src/api/data_contract.py blend + refresh/audit workflows
title: The pick-year discount double-counts: it applies 0.82/0.66 on top of retail pick values that already price the year
evidence: `config/weights/pick_year_discount.json` sets `offsetDiscounts {"1": 0.82, "2": 0.66, "3": 0.53}`, applied multiplicatively at `src/api/data_contract.py:6003-6032` (`_apply_pick_year_discount_to_blend`). The inputs are the vendors' OWN year-labelled pick rows, which already embed the market's time pricing — and this year they price it the OPPOSITE way: `CSVs/site_raw/ktcSfTep.csv` has `2026 Early 1st,5595` and `2027 Early 1st,7061`; `CSVs/site_raw/idpTradeCalc.csv` has `2026 Early 1st,5554.0` and `2027 Early 1st,7052.0`. Reproduced numerically end-to-end: n=2 mean(7061, 7052) = 7056.5, ×0.82 = 5786.3 → live board stamps `2027 Early 1st` at `rankDerivedValue = 5786`, `pickYearDiscount = 0.82`, `pickProjectedDraftValue = 7056` — an exact match. Same for 2028: mean(5122, 5034) = 5078.0, ×0.66 = 3351 → live value 3351. The function docstring at `:6045-6047` asserts "a 2027 1st today is 82% of a 2026 1.01 because of one year of uncertainty", which the two live markets contradict (they price it at 126% of the 2026 equivalent). Repo-wide grep for a backtest or calibration of these constants returns nothing.
userImpact: Every future-year pick on the board is 18% (2027) to 47% (2029) below what both retail markets that priced it agree on. This flows into the trade calculator, trade suggestions, the arbitrage finder and the draft board. A user trading away 2027/2028 firsts is being told they are cheaper than any market says they are — the platform will systematically approve selling future picks below market.
